reason: The hypothesis proposes a specific high-temperature (700–900 °C) hot-corrosion mechanism for bare Q235 steel involving salt-induced porous, non-adherent oxide spallation, which is not reported in any passage. The passages cover room-temperature salt spray, acid inhibition, passivation in concrete pore solution, and high-temperature corrosion of Ni-Cr-Mo claddings on Q235, but none study the bare Q235 steel under aggressive salt deposits at 700–900 °C. The hypothesis therefore goes beyond the literature by transferring the concept of chloride-induced scale degradation to a new, unstudied regime for this material.
